pages.text: It was Christmas Eve. The little tree in Azi's room glimmered softly in the corner, its lights casting warm patterns on the walls. Candles flickered on the dresser, and ornaments caught the gentle light. Through the frosted windowpanes, snow drifted lazily outside, quieting the world.

Azi was fast asleep in his wooden bed, curled up under a green checkered blanket with his favorite pillow, Jujy, tucked close. Jujy wasn't an ordinary pillow. Soft and black-and-white like a tuxedo cat, he had been with Azi for every story, every laugh, and every snuggle.

A red Christmas stocking hung nearby, and snowflake decorations sparkled on the walls. Tonight, watching Azi smile in his sleep, Jujy wished more than anything that he could give Azi a special Christmas gift - something magical, something perfect.

As the clock struck midnight, golden Christmas magic filled the air. Jujy felt a familiar tingling - his stitched eyes blinked open, his plush form beginning to change. This wasn't the first time - Azi never knew, but every Christmas Eve, magic transformed Jujy from a pillow into a real cat.

Where the soft pillow had been, now sat a black and white cat with bright eyes and whiskers that sparkled with starlight. Jujy stretched gracefully, adjusting the red snowflake cape that had appeared around his shoulders.
"Tonight's the night," he whispered excitedly. "I'll find the perfect gift for Azi!"

Padding silently to the window, Jujy saw houses dressed in holiday finery - wreaths with red bows adorned every door, and twinkling lights draped from snow-covered eaves. A warm golden glow seemed to beckon him forward, like a path of starlight waiting to be followed.

Following the golden light, Jujy found himself whisked away to a warm and bustling place. Rows of workbenches stretched out before him, stacked with colorful toys and glittering ribbons. Elves scurried about, and their laughter filled the air.
"Santa's Workshop," Jujy whispered, his soft voice filled with wonder. "Surely I'll find the perfect gift here!"

Santa stepped forward, his red coat shimmering like fresh snow. "Ah, Jujy," he said warmly. "Out searching for something special?" "Yes, Santa! I want to give Azi the most perfect Christmas gift ever. Something magical!"
Santa smiled kindly and handed Jujy a glowing golden compass. "This compass follows your heart, guiding you to what matters most," he explained. "Trust where it leads you."

Jujy landed softly in the snow, the compass pulsing with a warm light. It pointed him toward the small bus stop where Mama catches the 115 bus to work every morning. Azi and Papa always wait there with her, sharing morning hugs and kisses.
"Maybe I'll find the perfect gift here," Jujy thought, remembering how Azi would wave goodbye until Mama got on the bus and the bus drove out of sight before he and Papa went to school.
He didn't find the gift for Azi. All he found were sweet memories of morning kisses and "I love you"s that lingered long after Mama's bus departed.

The compass swirled and led Jujy to the Library, its magical walls and windows glowing warmly in the moonlight. Through the massive windows, he could see the cozy children's reading room where he and Azi spent countless Friday afternoons and Saturday mornings with Mama.
"This is where stories come alive," Jujy thought, remembering Azi's wide eyes during storytime, the quiet rustle of pages turning, the way Mama's voice would change for each character.
He remembered how tightly Azi would hold the books while discovering new adventures, excited to turn the pages.
The compass spun again, pointing toward the next destination. But as Jujy continued, the gentle snow turned into a whirling storm. The wind howled around him, whipping snow into his face.

His soft pillow body wasn't made for this weather, and his red snowflake cape kept trying to blow away. "Maybe I should go back," Jujy thought, huddling against a lamppost. He missed the warmth of Azi's room.
But he remembered how Azi had faced his fears at swim class - how he'd closed his mouth and tried until he could go under.
"If Azi can be brave learning to swim," Jujy whispered to himself, straightening his cape, "I have to be brave too!"
Holding the compass tightly, Jujy pushed through the storm. Each step was harder than the last, but he kept thinking of how strong Azi is, and how he needs to be strong too.
Finally, the storm began to calm, and through the swirling snowflakes, Jujy saw the familiar lights of the swim school glowing ahead.

The compass spun and pointed toward the swim school, its windows glowing softly in the night. This was where every Sunday morning, Mama and Papa watched proudly as Azi conquered fears and learned to float, then kick, then swim.
"Surely there's something special here," Jujy thought, remembering the triumph in Azi's voice calling "Did you see me?" after each new achievement.
He remembered how tightly Azi hugged Mama and Papa after learning to put his face in the water, how they dried Azi's happy tears after swimming the whole pool.

Just around the corner from the swim school, the compass led Jujy to the little bakery where they always went after class. Even in the middle of the night, the air still held traces of the warm flour and butter of all the baked goodies.

"This is where we celebrate," Jujy thought, remembering countless Sunday mornings: Azi's damp hair dripping on his shoulders, the proud choice of a croissant, the way Mama would break the croissant in half to share.
Every triumph, no matter how small, was honored here with flaky pastries, matcha, and cappuccinos.
Finally, the compass led Jujy to an unfamiliar station. "Sunset Park," read the sign above, as the R train rumbled by.
The platform was quiet now, dusted with snow, but somehow it felt important.
"I've never been here with Azi," Jujy thought, puzzled. But as he sat on the wooden bench, the compass glowed its warmest yet.
This was where Mama and Papa had lived before Azi was born. They fell in love in Brooklyn.
This was where Azi had first been part of their story, safe in Mama's belly as she waited for trains.
And suddenly Jujy understood - he wasn't just part of Azi's present moments, but connected to all the love that had come before, all the moments that had made their family what it was.
Jujy followed the compass one last time, through streets glowing with holiday warmth, until he reached their familiar green house.
Golden light spilled from every window, and wreaths with red bows decorated the snow-dusted front.
His paw prints in the fresh snow marked the final steps of his night's journey, each one bringing him closer to where he truly belonged - home with Azi.
When morning came, Jujy was right next to Azi - ready for a warm Christmas morning hug.

Mama and Papa and Azi all went down to the living room, where the grand Christmas tree stood proud by the tall window, its star reaching toward the ceiling, ornaments catching and scattering golden light.
Azi settled on the floor in his red plaid pajamas. Now Jujy finally understood what the compass had been showing him all along.
The gift wasn't something to be found anywhere. The gift was being there: for morning goodbyes and afternoon hellos, for learning and growing, for swim adventures and Sunday croissants.
Every moment, big and small, that made up their life together - that was the most perfect present of all.
As snow fell softly outside, string lights twinkled overhead, casting warm patterns on the walls.
The magic of Christmas morning sparkled in every corner, but the real magic, Jujy knew, was in the love they shared every single day of the year.

vocab.kidDefinition: shined with a soft twinkly light that comes and goes
the long thin hairs on a cat's face that help it feel where it is going
so full of people hurrying around that the whole place feels wide awake
ran with quick little steps, the way a mouse does
a small round tool with a spinning needle that shows you which way to go
the big proud feeling you get when you finally do the hard thing
a curly buttery roll that crackles into crumbs when you bite it
stayed a little longer, the way a hug stays after it ends
